reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space with its associated norm, let f:E→ℝ, X:ℝ→E, z∈E and T∈ℝ. Assume T≥0, f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on E, f is convex on all of E, and z is a global minimizer of f. Assume X is continuous on [0,T], including relative endpoint continuity, and for every t∈[0,T) the right derivative of X at t, taken within [t,∞), exists and equals −∇f(X(t)). Define L(t)=t²‖∇f(X(t))‖²+2t(f(X(t))−f(z))+‖X(t)−z‖². Then L is nonincreasing on [0,T]: for every a,b∈[0,T] with a≤b, L(b)≤L(a). Moreover, for every t∈(0,T], both ‖∇f(X(t))‖²≤‖X(0)−z‖²/t² and f(X(t))−f(z)≤‖X(0)−z‖²/(4t). The gradient is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative. No derivative assumption at T is required. For T=0, the rate assertions have empty time domain and the monotonicity assertion is on a singleton. No finite-dimensionality, positive lower bound on T, uniqueness of z or X, Lipschitz constant, or existence assertion for a trajectory is included.
